note: Derived from RequirementRegister.for_phase("15"): 11 MANDATORY requirements owned by control.specification (9) and control.policy (2, ARK-REQ-0390/0391). Phase 15 was a genuine canonical gap before D-025 (docs/build/DECISION_LOG.md): zero requirements, zero contract, zero bounded context, zero MS elaboration, confirmed by read-only research before any entry existed. D-025 repaired the gap by adding REQUIREMENT_REGISTER.md Block 8 (ARK-REQ-0381-0391), CONTRACT_INVENTORY.md C-37, and extending control.specification's concerns (requirement_and_architecture_intelligence) rather than creating a second bounded context.

claims.implementation: blueprint_engine.decompose/derive_blueprint accepts a human product goal (ProductGoal) and deterministically splits it into candidate requirement statements by enumeration markers or sentence boundaries.
claims.evidence: integ: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_engine.py::TestDecomposition proves determinism and both splitting rules. integ: backend/tests/specification/test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_2_a_real_goal_decomposes_with_provenance composes the real journey. prop: TestDeterministicRepeatability proves identical input always yields an identical blueprint.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: ProductGoal.goal_id and CandidateRequirement.requirement_id are content addresses (kernel.contracts.content_address) over the goal text and (index, statement) respectively, so every derived requirement's provenance traces back to the exact submitted bytes.
claims.evidence: prov: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_contracts.py::TestProductGoalProvenance. integ: test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_2 asserts every requirement_id is a real content address.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: derive_blueprint detects AMBIGUOUS (lexical marker), UNDERSPECIFIED (short/vague-unquantified) and MISSING_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA per statement, and CONTRADICTORY across statements sharing a constraint subject with disagreeing numeric values; every detection becomes an UnresolvedQuestion, never a silently invented resolution.
claims.evidence: integ: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_engine.py::TestDeriveBlueprintNegativeControls (6 cases: empty input refused, underspecified, ambiguous, contradictory detected, agreeing constraints NOT flagged, nothing invented for an unresolved statement). prop: test_nothing_is_silently_invented_for_an_unresolved_statement.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: derive_acceptance_criteria extracts a criterion only from a modal-anchored statement (must/shall/should) carrying an explicit numeric constraint pattern; every other statement yields an empty tuple and a MISSING_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA question.
claims.evidence: contract: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_engine.py::TestAcceptanceCriteriaDerivation (quantified/unquantified/no-modal cases). integ: test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_4 proves at least one real derivation over the composed journey.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: classify() matches a closed eight-member vocabulary (RequirementCategory, seven categories plus UNCLASSIFIED) via keyword sets; a statement matching no keyword stays UNCLASSIFIED rather than defaulting to a guessed member.
claims.evidence: contract: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_engine.py::TestClassification, parametrised over all seven derivable categories plus the unclassified case. unit: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_contracts.py proves RequirementCategory is a closed enum.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: map_architecture scores every concern in the live AuthorityMap.concerns by shared word tokens against the requirement's text/category and returns the highest-scoring live concern name or None; no category-to-owner table exists in the module, so the owner is always resolved live.
claims.evidence: arch: backend/tests/structural/test_requirement_blueprint_authority.py::TestArchitectureCompositionIsLiveNotDuplicated proves no bounded-context owner name is hard-coded anywhere in blueprint_engine.py. integ: test_blueprint_engine.py::TestArchitectureMapping and test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_5 compose the real AuthorityMap.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied. Composes control.architecture via a new declared sibling edge (control.specification -> control.architecture, D-025), not a same-layer violation.

claims.implementation: derive_blueprint's single composed entry point produces a RequirementBlueprint (C-37), a JSON-serializable Pydantic model. Phase 15 executes no generation itself.
claims.evidence: contract: backend/tests/specification/test_blueprint_contracts.py proves the model shape. integ: test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_6_the_blueprint_is_a_phase_16_consumable_interface proves a real model_dump_json/model_validate_json round trip.
claims.note: Both register evidence keys are supplied.

claims.implementation: derive_blueprint and every function in blueprint_engine.py perform no filesystem or process I/O and define no generation/build/write operation; product/software generation remains Phase 16's (engineering.factory, unbuilt) sole responsibility.
claims.evidence: arch: backend/tests/structural/test_requirement_blueprint_authority.py::TestNoFilesystemOrProcessIO and TestNoForeignAuthorityIsImported (no engineering.factory/candidate import). sec: test_phase_15_journey.py::test_step_9_deriving_a_blueprint_writes_no_file_and_generates_no_code proves it behaviourally against the real shipping tree.
claims.note: Owned by control.policy, the actor-boundary authority, matching the ARK-REQ-0212/0240 shape — the same structural reason ARK-REQ-0051 is owned by control.policy rather than the acting context.
